maria: Heads-up — after quantizing an HF checkpoint (GPT-style, GPTQ->int8) we started getting tool-call parsing failures in the Redwood conversion layer. appears to be a tokenizer/sentinel collision. :thinking:
kevin: Can you paste the failing snippet and the conversion step?
anita: saw similar once when a special token wasn't registered before tokenization. usually a missing special_tokens entry.
maria: Minimal repro (snipped):
```
# conversion step (pseudo)
text = user_prompt + TOOL_TAG_START + json.dumps(tool_call) + TOOL_TAG_END
tokens = tokenizer.encode(text)
# after quant / compaction some sentinel tokens split across bytes
# tokenizer.decode(tokens) -> '... >>>J', 'SONMODE<<< ...' which breaks JSON-mode detector
```
maria: On the failing model, tokenizer.encode sometimes splits our JSONMODE sentinel across token boundaries, so the post-process regex for JSON-mode doesn't match. Same run on fp16 model is fine.
kevin: That suggests tokenization differences introduced by quantization artifacts or different vocab alignment after conversion. But tokenizers shouldn't change with quantization — are we running a different tokenizer binary/version during the compile step?
maria: Good call — we were accidentally using the model's HF tokenizer vs. the conversion-tool's cached tokenizer (different pre-tokenizer settings). The conversion pipeline applied byte-pair merges from the model archive but didn't add our role/tool special tokens to the tokenizer config.json before saving.
sam: Quick fix options: 1) ensure all Redwood special tokens (JSONMODE sentinel, TOOL_TAG_{START,END}, ROLE_SYS/ASSISTANT/USER) are registered in tokenizer.special_tokens before saving model artifacts; 2) fall back to a safer splitter when detecting partial sentinel sequences; 3) add a canonical post-token-join step to repair split sentinels.
kevin: We should prefer (1) for correctness. Adding the special tokens to config.json -> "added_tokens" and re-save the tokenizer fixes deterministic encoding.
anita: Also add a unit test in eng-ml that encodes a suite of prompt templates (tool-calls + nested json) and asserts the sentinel appears as a single token.
ci-bot: [ci] nightly-inference-tests: started for branch/model/quant-int8 (build 4321) :gear:
maria: FYI eval numbers from the regression run:
- baseline (fp16): tool extraction pass rate 98.7%, mean latency 230ms
- quant-int8 (broken): tool extraction pass rate 83.4%, mean latency 195ms
Quality impact >15% relative drop in tool parse success — unacceptable.
kevin: Latency improvement nice but not at the cost of integrity. We need a small compatibility shim in the conversion CLI that ensures tokenizers get the special tokens mapped before any encode ops. Also log a warning if any sentinel is split across top-k tokens.
sam: Proposal: conversion CLI behavior
```
1) load hf tokenizer
2) add_special_tokens({"additional_special_tokens": ["<|jsonmode|>", "<|tool_start|>", "<|tool_end|>", "<|role_sys|>"]})
3) save tokenizer + config.json
4) run tokenization sanity checks on sample templates
```
anita: I'll add the unit test + a regression entry to the eval harness (add a toolcall prompt suite) — assigning to @anita.
maria: I've pinned a minimal repro and logs in the ticket: https://redwood.internal/issue/ML-721 (contains token dumps and failing parses).
kevin: I'll add conversion CLI guardrails and a small monitor in runtime to detect split-sentinel occurrences at runtime (emit metric rw.toolcall.sentinel.split_count).
sam: We should also include a short note in onboarding docs for HF model brings: "always register Redwood tool/role special tokens before saving tokenizer to HF archive". I can PR that to docs/devex.

maria: Thanks — next steps: anita unit tests + PR, kevin conversion CLI change, sam docs note. I'll re-run the quant-int8 eval once conversion updates are in. :thumbsup:
